subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should deferred maintenance preserve the existing per-session plugin invocation serialization after a timeout, or should OpenClaw intentionally make concurrent same-session `maintain()` calls a required plugin contract?
rationale: The patch currently chooses a compatibility-sensitive public plugin API behavior: it releases a host lane while allowing the previous plugin invocation to continue. Choosing whether the core must preserve serialization or whether all engines must adopt a new concurrency contract requires maintainer ownership of the SDK behavior.

options.title: Preserve core serialization
options.body: Keep the user-turn release and host fencing, but defer or coalesce later maintenance until the abandoned same-session invocation settles.

options.title: Adopt concurrent maintenance
options.body: Accept the new plugin contract, explicitly announce the compatibility change, and require broad engine audit and upgrade evidence before merge.

recommendation.title: Preserve core serialization
recommendation.body: Keep the user-turn release and host fencing, but defer or coalesce later maintenance until the abandoned same-session invocation settles.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor owns the proposed lifecycle design in this PR and can incorporate the selected direction; current-main area ownership was not established from the available evidence.
